channel.title: World of Wonders Blog
channel.description: Stories, Gita, festivals and Vedic Maths for families

item.title: Lift Yourself: Meera's Bicycle and Bhagavad Gita 6.5 for Children
item.description: A short story of a girl learning to ride a bicycle, what Bhagavad Gita 6.5 says about the mind as our best friend or worst enemy, and one small step for children and families.

item.title: Steady Hands in the Storm: The Potter, Calm Action and Bhagavad Gita 2.48
item.description: A short story of a potter who keeps his hands steady in a storm, what Bhagavad Gita 2.48 says about samatvam (evenness of mind), and one calm-action step for children and families.

item.title: Bali Padyami Story for Children: King Bali, Vamana and the Promise of Three Steps
item.description: The story of King Bali and Vamana told for children, why Bali Padyami is celebrated after Deepavali in Karnataka and Maharashtra, its link with Onam, and a simple promise activity for families.

item.title: Why Do We Light Diyas on Deepavali? Rama's Return to Ayodhya, Told for Children
item.description: The story of Rama's return to Ayodhya, why Deepavali means a row of lamps, the five days of the festival, and a simple diya activity for children and parents.

item.title: Run From Fear and It Chases You: Swami Vivekananda, the Monkeys and Bhagavad Gita 2.3
item.description: The story of Swami Vivekananda and the monkeys of Banaras, what Bhagavad Gita 2.3 says about fear, and one small step children and parents can take today.
